title: "Restrictions on the report family"

description: "Consequences of grade caps, exact grade counts and fixed-order restrictions for minimum risk."
---

Minimum reporting risk depends on which grade reports are allowed: all reports, at most *G* grades, exactly *G* occupied grades, or contiguous cuts of one declared unit order.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Exactly six.** Across 720 strict rankings, minimum risk is .0480 versus .0372 unrestricted.
- **At most three.** Both the 603 capped reports and 540 three-grade reports reach .0417.
- **B before A.** Cutting the declared order searches 32 reports at risk .0379 versus .0372.
- **Two criteria.** Among 24 strict orders, 75 total reports, and 8 cuts, four grades cost 7/40.
- **A dominating set.** At τ = 4/9, unrestricted optima cost 4/15 while a two-grade cap costs 17/54.

<details>
<summary>Family nesting and tie rules</summary>

At a fixed withholding cost, enlarging the allowed family can only lower the minimum risk or leave it unchanged. The dashed mark gives the risk of withholding every pair; requiring multiple occupied grades excludes that report. Equal-risk ties and the fixed-order dynamic program's tie rule appear in **Data and family search details**. All examples are specified for teaching.

</details>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
sc <- postrank_expected_rank(pr_tutorial$one)
postrank_cuts(sc, pr_tutorial$one, postrank_settings(weights=c(score_A=1), tau=.2, G_max=6L, exact_G=6L), rule="optimal")$risk
```
This cuts the expected-rank order; its result agrees with the exact-count optimum here.
:::

Standalone: [families](../../embed/families.html), for example `?family=exact&G=2&tau=.40`.
